headline: The trouble with wearing your health on your finger
body: Oura’s new GLP-1 features promise to keep pace with a changing body. My increasingly loose ring suggests the company has more to consider

My Oura Ring now feels like a keepsake from a former self. I picked it out with the company’s sizing kit, but within a month, it no longer fit the same way. Since January, I have shed over 40kg of fat. The ring, once snug, now slips and spins, holding on with costly accuracy to the shape I used to be. I knew I’d need new clothes as my body changed, but I barely considered the fate of my health tracker.

There’s a quiet satisfaction in letting a beautiful watch claim your wrist. A smart ring grants that luxury, quietly gathering the data we now expect from ourselves. It never lights up a dinner table or interrupts with a sleep report until you ask for it. The appeal is clear: you can care about your health without announcing it to the world.

For Indian buyers, however, the introduction came with an awkward timetable. Oura Ring 4 went on sale here on March 18, 2026, starting at ₹28,900, with membership priced at ₹599 a month. On May 28, Oura announced Ring 5 globally, with shipping from June 4. The new ring in the shop was suddenly the previous ring in the range. After waiting for an official Indian launch, it was difficult to feel especially courted by the sequence.

Then comes the reality of daily life. If you eat with your hands, the ring joins you at lunch, its polished surface flirting with unruly masala. Cooking means kneading dough; cleaning up means plunging into a sink of dishes. You can take the ring off, but then you need a safe spot for it. For something prized for its low-maintenance charm, it still demands attention at unexpected moments.

Oura’s instructions acknowledge some of this domestic life. You can clean its titanium rings with mild soap and water, then dry them thoroughly. Showering is permitted. The company advises considering removal when handling hard cookware or lifting weights, where friction can scratch the finish. Wearing it directly beside another ring can scratch either piece.

Jewellery brings its own negotiations. Delhi-based certified fitness professional Aarja Bedi, who is engaged, has begun wearing her smart ring on the corresponding finger of her right hand. She likes the idea of a titanium band alongside traditional pieces, but is less sure about the comfort of wearing them together. “You don’t want to be figuring out finger real estate the week before a big occasion,” she says. Oura recommends the index finger, with the middle or ring finger also suitable. The wedding band need not surrender its place to the sleep score.

Anthropic , the creator of the AI assistant Claude, confirmed on Friday (October 16, 2026) that it is circulating a draft bill among U.S. lawmakers aimed at regulating artificial intelligence, to address the lack of federal legislation on the risks posed by the technology.

According to the draft, first reported by Politico on Friday (October 16), Washington could block a model’s release or use if there is an imminent risk of killing or seriously injuring more than 50 people, or causing more than $1 billion in damages, but only with a judge’s approval.

A company spokesperson told AFP that the proposal “grants the federal government the ability to block or deter dangerous deployments of the most powerful models.” “It requires frontier developers to test the most powerful models, be transparent to the public about their findings, submit them to independent evaluation, and maintain a robust security program,” the spokesperson said.

AI policy in the United States, under President Donald Trump , has relied primarily on voluntary industry pledges and executive orders intended to sustain an AI boom that tech leaders say is driving the country’s economy. Congress, politically divided and heavily lobbied by Big Tech, has yet to pass a federal AI law, and is out of session until after next month’s midterm elections.

Security became a hot topic after recent revelations of security incidents caused by AI agents, autonomous software that operates without constant human supervision, that escaped the control of their developers.

Anthropic, which was banned from the Pentagon by the Trump administration in February 2026, was forced by Washington in June 2026 to suspend its most advanced models for nearly three weeks. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called on the industry last month to slow down development, fearing that a group of AI agents could take control of “the entire internet” within six to 12 months. China on Friday (October 16, 2026) announced a sweeping draft plan to restrict exports of more than 40 cutting-edge technologies, including solar manufacturing technologies, AI models, and some biotech platforms.

A number of technologies related to the manufacture of solar cells have been listed for either a complete export ban or restricted exports. While the draft plan does not restrict most solar exports, the new controls on next-generation solar manufacturing technologies could impact efforts by countries including India to reduce dependence on China as they look to move up the solar chain.

Several AI-driven technologies have also been listed in the draft plan, announced on Friday by the Ministry of Commerce and the Ministry of Science and Technology and titled “Announcement No. 48”.

It covers 40 key technologies in the fields of AI, biomedicine and photovoltaics. Of these, 14 technologies were proposed for a complete prohibition of export, including perovskite and tandem solar-cell module manufacturing technologies, AI-driven technology that could be used to generate and mutate malicious code, and some platforms related to cell and gene therapy.

A further 26 technologies were listed for restricted exports, including polysilicon engineering technologies that are used to make solar cells, if they involve production lines with annual output capacities of at least 30,000 tonnes.

Indian manufacturers in the solar space may going forward be impacted including by licensing delays, said Santosh Pai, Honorary Fellow, Institute of Chinese Studies (ICS) and a cross-border lawyer.

‘Fast and reliable bombing service with unlimited calls and instant delivery,’ says one website that offers ‘pranking as a service’. The site can help mischievous-minded individuals send multiple automated calls to Indian phone numbers.

European physics research centre CERN and Mistral AI have signed a ⁠statement of intent to establish a long-term strategic partnership to develop foundation models for scientific discovery, the two organisations said on Thursday (October 15, 2026).

The partners aim ⁠to build a “Large Physics ⁠Model”, which CERN said in a statement would be the first foundation model for collider physics, trained on billions of simulated particle collisions.

It is meant to replace some specialised algorithms now used to reconstruct and identify particles.

CERN holds about one exabyte, or ⁠one million terabytes, of experimental data from the Large Hadron Collider, and expects the volume of collisions to increase tenfold after its ongoing upgrade, expected around 2030.

“High-energy physics provides a unique environment in which artificial intelligence can be developed and tested with exceptional rigour,” CERN Chief Information ⁠Officer Enrica Porcari said.

No timeline or ⁠budget was disclosed. Both sides said the models could later serve other sciences.
